slot.brief: For a gas-phase reaction with given Δn, state whether ΔH is greater than, less than or equal to ΔU and why.

stem: For the gas-phase reaction $\text{N}_2(g)+\text{O}_2(g)\rightarrow 2\text{NO}(g)$, which statement is correct?
options: $\text{Δ}H=\text{Δ}U$, since the change in moles of gas is zero.
$\text{Δ}H>\text{Δ}U$, since there are more gaseous product molecules.
$\text{Δ}H<\text{Δ}U$, since the reactants have more gaseous moles.
$\text{Δ}H\ne\text{Δ}U$, since every gas-phase reaction has a nonzero gas-mole change.

verdicts.working: For ideal gases, ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT. Here Δn_g = 2 − (1 + 1) = 0, so ΔH = ΔU.

working:
$\text{Δ}n_{\text{g}}=2-(1+1)=0$
$\text{Δ}H=\text{Δ}U+\text{Δ}n_{\text{g}}RT=\text{Δ}U$

Independent check: For ideal gases, ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT. Here Δn_g = 2 − (1 + 1) = 0, so ΔH = ΔU.
